# star_toml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/star-toml/26.7.2/star_toml/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#star_toml--load-layer-and-validate-any-toml-config-file)star_toml — load, layer, and validate any `*.toml` config file

`star_toml` (pronounced “star TOML”, as in `*.toml`) is a self-contained
Rust framework for any TOML configuration file. Three concerns, one crate:

- **Loading**— parse a single file, compose multiple sources in layers, expand- `${ENV_VARS}`, walk parent dirs to discover config files.
- **Validation**— Pydantic-style engine that collects- *every*error at once, each with a path-precise location, the offending value, and a machine-matchable code.
- **Analytics**— Van der Aalst-grade extensions: conformance fitness, variant fingerprinting, DECLARE cross-field constraints, severity stratification.

Dependencies: `serde`, `toml`, `thiserror`. No async, no proc-macros, no allocator
tricks, no crypto.

[§](https://docs.rs#decision-guide--which-api-for-which-task)Decision guide — which API for which task?

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| Parse a TOML string | `from_str::<T>(s)` |
| Load one file | `load_file::<T>(path)` |
| Walk parent dirs to find a file | /`find_config_file``find_and_load` |
| Merge defaults + file + env | builder`Loader` |
| Remember where the file is (relative paths) | →`Loader::load_file``ConfigFile<T>` |
| Parse + validate in one call | `Loader::load_validated` |
| Serialize back to TOML | /`to_string``save_file` |
| Recursive table merge | `deep_merge` |
| `${VAR}`substitution alone | `expand_env_vars` |
| Validate an already-loaded struct | /`Validate::check``Validate::validated` |
| Validate without a Rust struct | declarative builder`Schema` |
| Attach severity / cross-field rules | /`Validator::with_severity``Validator::check_consistent` |
| Get conformance score | `ValidationErrors::fitness` |
| Fingerprint error pattern | `ValidationErrors::variant_id` |

[§](https://docs.rs#complete-public-api)Complete public API

[§](https://docs.rs#loading)Loading

| Symbol | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from_str` | fn | Expand env vars, parse TOML, deserialize to `T` |
| `load_file` | fn | Read, expand, parse a `.toml`file |
| `find_config_file` | fn | Walk parent dirs for `name`; returns`Option<PathBuf>` |
| `find_and_load` | fn | +`find_config_file`combined`load_file` |
| `Loader` | struct | Builder: chain `.layer_str`,`.find_file`,`.env_prefix`, then`.load()` |
| `ConfigFile<T>` | struct | Loaded config + path; `.resolve(rel)`anchors relative paths |
| `to_string` | fn | Serialize `T: Serialize`to a TOML string |
| `save_file` | fn | Serialize to disk, creating parent dirs as needed |
| `deep_merge` | fn | Recursively merge two `toml::Value`s (later wins) |
| `expand_env_vars` | fn | `${VAR}`/`$VAR`substitution; unknown vars left intact |

[§](https://docs.rs#validation-pydantic--van-der-aalst)Validation (Pydantic + Van der Aalst)

| Symbol | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Schema` | struct | Declarative builder: validate `toml::Value`/ TOML strings without a Rust struct |
| `FieldBuilder` | struct | Fluent constraint chain returned by `Schema::field` |
| `Validate` | trait | Implement `validate(&self, v: &mut Validator)`on your config type |
| `Validator` | struct | Accumulates errors; carries the current path location |
| `Validator::field` | method | Descend into table key `name`for the duration of a closure |
| `Validator::index` | method | Descend into array index `i`for the duration of a closure |
| `Validator::with_severity` | method | Set for all checks inside a closure`Severity` |
| `Validator::check_non_empty` | method | Fail if `&str`is empty → code`empty` |
| `Validator::check_range` | method | Fail if value outside `lo..=hi`→ code`out_of_range` |
| `Validator::check_one_of` | method | Fail if value not in allowed set → code `not_one_of` |
| `Validator::check_predicate` | method | Custom boolean check with caller-defined code |
| `Validator::check_consistent` | method | DECLARE cross-field constraint → code `Inconsistent` |
| `Validator::error` | method | Record a raw at the current location`ErrorKind` |
| `Validator::error_with` | method | Same, capturing the offending value as a string |
| `Validator::finish` | method | Consume validator → `Ok(())`or`Err(ValidationErrors)` |
| `ValidationErrors` | struct | Non-empty collection of failures; implements `Display`+`Error` |
| `ValidationErrors::errors` | method | Slice of individual s`ValidationError` |
| `ValidationErrors::len` | method | Error count |
| `ValidationErrors::fitness` | method | Conformance score: `checks_passed / checks_run`(0.0–1.0) |
| `ValidationErrors::variant_id` | method | FNV-1a fingerprint of the error pattern |
| `ValidationErrors::by_section` | method | Group errors by top-level config section |
| `ValidationErrors::has_fatal` | method | True if any error is `Severity::Fatal` |
| `ValidationErrors::errors_above` | method | Filter to errors at or above a severity level |
| `ValidationError` | struct | One failure: `loc`,`kind`,`severity`,`input`,`msg` |
| `ValidationError::code` | method | Stable string code ( `"empty"`,`"out_of_range"`, …) |
| `ValidationError::repair_hint` | method | Auto-derived minimum fix for this error kind |
| `ValidationError::is_fatal` | method | True when `severity == Severity::Fatal` |
| `ErrorKind` | enum | Structured reason: `Empty`,`OutOfRange`,`NotOneOf`,`Inconsistent`, … |
| `Loc` | struct | Path into the config tree, e.g. `server.tls.port`or`[2].name` |
| `LocSegment` | enum | `Key(String)`or`Index(usize)` |
| `Severity` | enum | `Advisory`<`Warning`<`Error`<`Fatal` |

[§](https://docs.rs#error-types)Error types

| Variant | When |
|---|---|
| `Error::FileNotFound` | File does not exist |
| `Error::Io` | OS error reading / writing a file |
| `Error::Parse` | TOML syntax or serde deserialization error |
| `Error::Serialize` | `toml::to_string`failed |
| `Error::Invalid` | Wraps ; returned by`ValidationErrors``Loader::load_validated` |
| `Error::Validation` | Lower-level validation string; rarely produced by this crate |

[§](https://docs.rs#patterns-cookbook-copy-pasteable)Patterns cookbook (copy-pasteable)

[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-1--load-a-single-file)Pattern 1 — load a single file

```
use star_toml::load_file;
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct AppConfig { name: String, port: u16 }
let cfg: AppConfig = load_file("app.toml")?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-2--layered-loading-defaults--file--env)Pattern 2 — layered loading (defaults + file + env)

```
use star_toml::Loader;
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Cfg { name: String, port: u16 }
const DEFAULTS: &str = "name = 'my-app'\nport = 8080\n";
let cfg: Cfg = Loader::new()
    .layer_str(DEFAULTS, "built-in defaults")  // lowest priority
    .find_file("app.toml")                      // walk up from cwd
    .layer_file_if_exists("~/.config/app.toml") // optional user overrides
    .env_prefix("APP_")                         // APP_PORT=9090 → port = 9090
    .load()?;                                   // highest priority
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-3--load--validate-in-one-call)Pattern 3 — load + validate in one call

```
use star_toml::{Loader, Validate, Validator};
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Cfg { port: u16 }
impl Validate for Cfg {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
    }
}
// Fails with Error::Invalid(ValidationErrors) if any rule is violated.
let cfg: Cfg = Loader::new().find_file("server.toml").load_validated()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-4--collect-all-errors-render-pydantic-style)Pattern 4 — collect all errors, render Pydantic-style

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Server { host: String, port: u16 }
struct App { name: String, workers: u32, server: Server }
impl Validate for Server {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("host", &self.host);
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1..=65535);
    }
}
impl Validate for App {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_non_empty("name", &self.name);
        v.check_range("workers", self.workers, 1..=1024);
        v.field("server", |v| self.server.validate(v)); // nested → server.*
    }
}
let app = App {
    name: String::new(),
    workers: 0,
    server: Server { host: String::new(), port: 0 },
};
let report = app.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(report.len(), 4); // ALL four errors, not just the first
let locs: Vec<String> = report.errors().iter().map(|e| e.loc.to_string()).collect();
assert_eq!(locs, ["name", "workers", "server.host", "server.port"]);
// Renders as:
// 4 validation errors for App
// name
//   must not be empty (got: `""`) [empty]
// ...
println!("{report}");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-5--severity-levels--repair-hints)Pattern 5 — severity levels + repair hints

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator, Severity};
struct Cfg { log_dir: String, port: u16 }
impl Validate for Cfg {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        // Hard error: port is required
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
        // Advisory: non-critical best-practice hint
        v.with_severity(Severity::Advisory, |v| {
            v.check_non_empty("log_dir", &self.log_dir);
        });
    }
}
let errs = Cfg { port: 0, log_dir: String::new() }.check().unwrap_err();
assert!(!errs.has_fatal());
for e in errs.errors() {
    println!("[{}] {} → fix: {}", e.severity, e.loc, e.repair_hint());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-6--van-der-aalst-analytics)Pattern 6 — Van der Aalst analytics

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Pair { a: u32, b: u32 }
impl Validate for Pair {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("a", self.a, 1..=10); // passes
        v.check_range("b", self.b, 1..=10); // fails
    }
}
let errs = Pair { a: 5, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err();
// Conformance fitness: how much of the model the config satisfies
assert_eq!(errs.fitness(), 0.5); // 1 of 2 checks passed
// Variant fingerprint: same error pattern = same ID across runs
let id = errs.variant_id();
assert_eq!(Pair { a: 9, b: 0 }.check().unwrap_err().variant_id(), id);
// Object-centric grouping: errors by top-level config section
for (section, errors) in errs.by_section() {
    println!("{section}: {} error(s)", errors.len());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-7--declare-cross-field-constraint)Pattern 7 — DECLARE cross-field constraint

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Tls { enabled: bool, cert_path: String }
impl Validate for Tls {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        // Co-existence: TLS enabled ⟺ cert_path non-empty
        v.check_consistent(
            "cert_path",            // primary field (where error is recorded)
            &["enabled"],           // related fields (tagged in ErrorKind::Inconsistent)
            !self.enabled || !self.cert_path.is_empty(),
            "tls_cert_required",    // stable machine-matchable code
            "cert_path must be set when TLS is enabled",
        );
    }
}
let bad = Tls { enabled: true, cert_path: String::new() };
let errs = bad.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].code(), "tls_cert_required");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-8--validate-arrays-element-by-element)Pattern 8 — validate arrays element-by-element

```
use star_toml::{Validate, Validator};
struct Pipeline(Vec<String>);
impl Validate for Pipeline {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        for (i, stage) in self.0.iter().enumerate() {
            v.index(i, |v| v.check_non_empty("name", stage));
        }
    }
}
let p = Pipeline(vec!["build".into(), String::new(), "test".into()]);
let errs = p.check().unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(errs.errors()[0].loc.to_string(), "[1].name");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-9--source-relative-path-resolution)Pattern 9 — source-relative path resolution

```
use star_toml::{Loader, ConfigFile};
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Build { template_dir: String }
let cf: ConfigFile<Build> = Loader::new().find_file("build.toml").load_file()?;
// Resolved relative to the directory that contains build.toml,
// not relative to the current working directory.
let abs = cf.resolve(&cf.config.template_dir);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pattern-10--write-back)Pattern 10 — write-back

```
use star_toml::save_file;
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
struct Config { name: String, port: u16 }
save_file(&Config { name: "app".into(), port: 8080 }, "ggen.toml")?;
// Parent directories are created automatically.
```
[§](https://docs.rs#layer-merge-semantics)Layer merge semantics

Layers merge left-to-right (later = higher priority).

- **Tables**: keys merged recursively — a later layer overrides one key without erasing siblings.
- **Arrays, scalars**: later layer replaces earlier entirely.

```
use toml::Value;
use star_toml::deep_merge;
let mut base: Value = toml::from_str("[db]\nhost=\"localhost\"\nport=5432\n").unwrap();
let overlay: Value = toml::from_str("[db]\nport=5433\n").unwrap();
deep_merge(&mut base, overlay);
// host preserved, port overridden
assert_eq!(base["db"]["host"].as_str(), Some("localhost"));
assert_eq!(base["db"]["port"].as_integer(), Some(5433));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#environment-variable-mapping)Environment variable mapping

`.env_prefix("APP_")` maps env vars to TOML keys:

- Prefix stripped: `APP_PORT`→`port`
- Double underscore as dot: `APP_SERVER__PORT`→`server.port`
- Value coercion: `"true"`→ bool,`"42"`→ integer,`"3.14"`→ float, otherwise string

Inline `${VAR}` / `$VAR` patterns in TOML sources are expanded before parsing.
Unknown variables are left as-is (safe for partial expansion).

```
use star_toml::expand_env_vars;
std::env::set_var("MY_HOST", "prod.example.com");
let out = expand_env_vars("host = \"${MY_HOST}\"");
assert_eq!(out, "host = \"prod.example.com\"");
std::env::remove_var("MY_HOST");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling)Error handling

All fallible free functions return [ Result<T>](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html) =

`Result<T, Error>`.
The most common error is [from](https://docs.rs/error/enum.Error.html#variant.Invalid)

`Error::Invalid`[; downcast with](https://docs.rs/loader/struct.Loader.html#method.load_validated)

`Loader::load_validated``if let Error::Invalid(report) = err { … }`.```
use star_toml::{Loader, Validate, Validator, Error};
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Cfg { port: u16 }
impl Validate for Cfg {
    fn validate(&self, v: &mut Validator) {
        v.check_range("port", self.port, 1024..=65535);
    }
}
match Loader::new().find_file("server.toml").load_validated::<Cfg>() {
    Ok(cfg) => println!("port = {}", cfg.port),
    Err(Error::FileNotFound(p)) => eprintln!("config not found: {}", p.display()),
    Err(Error::Parse { source, .. }) => eprintln!("TOML syntax: {source}"),
    Err(Error::Invalid(report)) => {
        eprintln!("{report}");
        for e in report.errors() {
            eprintln!("  fix {} → {}", e.loc, e.repair_hint());
        }
    }
    Err(e) => eprintln!("other error: {e}"),
}
```

# zebra_state - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/zebra-state/10.0.0/zebra_state/

## Expand description

State contextual verification and storage code for Zebra.

[§](https://docs.rs#correctness)Correctness

Await UTXO and block commit requests should be wrapped in a timeout, because:

- await UTXO requests wait for a block containing that UTXO, and
- contextual verification and state updates wait for all previous blocks.

Otherwise, verification of out-of-order and invalid blocks can hang indefinitely.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [check_and_delete_old_databases](https://docs.rs/config/fn.check_and_delete_old_databases.html);
- `pub use config::`- [check_and_delete_old_state_databases](https://docs.rs/config/fn.check_and_delete_old_state_databases.html);
- `pub use config::`- [database_format_version_on_disk](https://docs.rs/config/fn.database_format_version_on_disk.html);
- `pub use config::`- [state_database_format_version_on_disk](https://docs.rs/config/fn.state_database_format_version_on_disk.html);
- `pub use config::`- [Config](https://docs.rs/config/struct.Config.html);
- `pub use constants::`- [state_database_format_version_in_code](https://docs.rs/constants/fn.state_database_format_version_in_code.html);

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [init_](https://docs.rs/fn.init_read_only.html)- read_ - only
- Initialize a read state service from the provided `Config`
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_init_read_only.html)- init_ - read_ - only
- Calls `init_read_only``Config``Network`

HashMap A hash map  implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup. HeadData  Parachain head data included in the chain. HrmpChannelId   A type that uniquely identifies an HRMP channel. An HRMP channel is established between two
paras. In text, we use the notation `(A, B)` to specify a channel between A and B. The channels
are unidirectional, meaning that `(A, B)` and `(B, A)` refer to different channels. The
convention is that we use the first item tuple for the sender and the second for the recipient.
Only one channel is allowed between two participants in one direction, i.e. there cannot be 2
different channels identified by `(A, B)`. A channel with the same para id in sender and
recipient is invalid. That is, however, not enforced. InboundMessagesData   The messages that are passed by the collator to the parachain runtime as part of the
inherent data. LazyLock  A value which is initialized on the first access. Location A relative path between state-bearing consensus systems. MessageQueuePallet   The `Pallet` struct, the main type that implements traits and standalone

Cranelift code generation library.

- Compact representation of `Option<T>`for types with a reserved value.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/struct.CallInfo.html)- Info
- Out-of-line data for calls, to keep the size of `Inst`down.
- [Compile](https://docs.rs/struct.CompileError.html)- Error
- Compilation error, with the accompanying function to help printing it.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)
- Persistent data structures and compilation pipeline.
- [Final](https://docs.rs/struct.Final.html)
- Status of a compiled artifact ready to use.
- [Finalized](https://docs.rs/struct.FinalizedMachCallSite.html)- Mach - Call - Site
- A call site record resulting from a compilation.
- [Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.FrameLayout.html)- Layout
- Structure describing the layout of a function’s stack frame.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html)- Buffer
- A buffer of output to be produced, fixed up, and then emitted to a CodeSink in bulk.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBufferDebugTagList.html)- Buffer - Debug - TagList
- Iterator item for visiting debug tags.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBufferFinalized.html)- Buffer - Finalized
- A `MachBuffer`once emission is completed: holds generated code and records, without fixups. This allows the type to be independent of the backend.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBufferFrameLayout.html)- Buffer - Frame - Layout
- Stack-frame layout information carried through to machine code. This provides sufficient information to interpret an active stack frame from a running function, if provided.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachCallSite.html)- Call - Site
- A call site record resulting from a compilation.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html)- Label
- A label refers to some offset in a `MachBuffer`. It may not be resolved at the point at which it is used by emitted code; the buffer records “fixups” for references to the label, and will come back and patch the code appropriately when the label’s location is eventually known.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachSrcLoc.html)- SrcLoc
- A source-location mapping resulting from a compilation.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachTextSectionBuilder.html)- Text - Section - Builder
- Implementation of the `TextSectionBuilder`trait backed by`MachBuffer`.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachTrap.html)- Trap
- A trap record resulting from a compilation.
- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenPatchRegion.html)- Patch - Region
- Represents the beginning of an editable region in the `MachBuffer``OpenPatchRegion``MachBuffer::end_patchable``OpenPatchRegion`
- [Patch](https://docs.rs/struct.PatchRegion.html)- Region
- A region in the `MachBuffer``MachBuffer::start_patchable``PatchRegion``MachBuffer::end_patchable``PatchRegion::patch`
- [RealReg](https://docs.rs/struct.RealReg.html)
- A real (physical) register. This corresponds to one of the target ISA’s named registers and can be used as an instruction operand.
- [Reg](https://docs.rs/struct.Reg.html)
- A register named in an instruction. This register can be a virtual
register, a fixed physical register, or a named spillslot (after
regalloc). It does not have any constraints applied to it: those
can be added later in `MachInst::get_operands()`when the`Reg`s are converted to`Operand`s.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.TakeAndReplace.html)- AndReplace
- An RAII type to temporarily take a `U`out of a`T`and then put it back again on drop.
- [VCode](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstant.html)- Constant
- A use of a constant by one or more VCode instructions; see [VCodeConstants](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstants.html).
- [VCode](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstants.html)- Constants
- This structure tracks the large constants used in VCode that will be emitted separately by the
[MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html).
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.ValueLocRange.html)- LocRange
- Value location range.
- [Writable](https://docs.rs/struct.Writable.html)
- A type wrapper that indicates a register type is writable. The
underlying register can be extracted, and the type wrapper can be
built using an arbitrary register. Hence, this type-level wrapper
is not strictly a guarantee. However, “casting” to a writable
register is an explicit operation for which we can
audit. Ordinarily, internal APIs in the compiler backend should
take a `Writable<Reg>`whenever the register is written, and the usual, frictionless way to get one of these is to allocate a new temporary.

### x86

This feature flag does not enable additional features.

# cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/index.html

## Expand description

Cranelift code generation library.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::verifier::`- [verify_function](https://docs.rs/verifier/fn.verify_function.html);
- `pub use crate::write::`- [write_function](https://docs.rs/write/fn.write_function.html);
- `pub use`- [cranelift_bforest](https://docs.rs/cranelift-bforest/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_bforest/index.html)as bforest;
- `pub use`- [cranelift_bitset](https://docs.rs/cranelift-bitset/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_bitset/index.html)as bitset;
- `pub use`- [cranelift_control](https://docs.rs/cranelift-control/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_control/index.html)as control;
- `pub use`- [cranelift_entity](https://docs.rs/cranelift-entity/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_entity/index.html)as entity;
- `pub use`- [gimli](https://docs.rs/gimli/0.33.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gimli/index.html);- `unwind`

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [binemit](https://docs.rs/binemit/index.html)
- Binary machine code emission.
- [cfg_](https://docs.rs/cfg_printer/index.html)- printer
- The `CFGPrinter`utility.
- [cursor](https://docs.rs/cursor/index.html)
- Cursor library.
- [data_](https://docs.rs/data_value/index.html)- value
- This module gives users to instantiate values that Cranelift understands. These values are used, for example, during interpretation and for wrapping immediates.
- [dbg](https://docs.rs/dbg/index.html)
- Debug tracing helpers.
- [dominator_](https://docs.rs/dominator_tree/index.html)- tree
- A Dominator Tree represented as mappings of Blocks to their immediate dominator.
- [flowgraph](https://docs.rs/flowgraph/index.html)
- A control flow graph represented as mappings of basic blocks to their predecessors and successors.
- [inline](https://docs.rs/inline/index.html)
- Function inlining infrastructure.
- [ir](https://docs.rs/ir/index.html)
- Representation of Cranelift IR functions.
- [isa](https://docs.rs/isa/index.html)
- Instruction Set Architectures.
- [loop_](https://docs.rs/loop_analysis/index.html)- analysis
- A loop analysis represented as mappings of loops to their header Block and parent in the loop tree.
- [packed_](https://docs.rs/packed_option/index.html)- option
- Compact representation of `Option<T>`for types with a reserved value.
- [print_](https://docs.rs/print_errors/index.html)- errors
- Utility routines for pretty-printing error messages.
- [settings](https://docs.rs/settings/index.html)
- Shared settings module.
- [timing](https://docs.rs/timing/index.html)
- Pass timing.
- [traversals](https://docs.rs/traversals/index.html)
- Traversals over the IR.
- [verifier](https://docs.rs/verifier/index.html)
- A verifier for ensuring that functions are well formed. It verifies:
- [write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html)
- Converting Cranelift IR to text.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [trace](https://docs.rs/macro.trace.html)
- Even when trace logging is disabled, the trace macro has a significant performance cost so we disable it by default.
- [trace_](https://docs.rs/macro.trace_log_enabled.html)- log_ - enabled
- Dynamic check for whether trace logging is enabled.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/struct.CallInfo.html)- Info
- Out-of-line data for calls, to keep the size of `Inst`down.
- [Compile](https://docs.rs/struct.CompileError.html)- Error
- Compilation error, with the accompanying function to help printing it.
- [Context](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html)
- Persistent data structures and compilation pipeline.
- [Final](https://docs.rs/struct.Final.html)
- Status of a compiled artifact ready to use.
- [Finalized](https://docs.rs/struct.FinalizedMachCallSite.html)- Mach - Call - Site
- A call site record resulting from a compilation.
- [Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.FrameLayout.html)- Layout
- Structure describing the layout of a function’s stack frame.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html)- Buffer
- A buffer of output to be produced, fixed up, and then emitted to a CodeSink in bulk.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBufferDebugTagList.html)- Buffer - Debug - TagList
- Iterator item for visiting debug tags.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBufferFinalized.html)- Buffer - Finalized
- A `MachBuffer`once emission is completed: holds generated code and records, without fixups. This allows the type to be independent of the backend.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBufferFrameLayout.html)- Buffer - Frame - Layout
- Stack-frame layout information carried through to machine code. This provides sufficient information to interpret an active stack frame from a running function, if provided.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachCallSite.html)- Call - Site
- A call site record resulting from a compilation.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html)- Label
- A label refers to some offset in a `MachBuffer`. It may not be resolved at the point at which it is used by emitted code; the buffer records “fixups” for references to the label, and will come back and patch the code appropriately when the label’s location is eventually known.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachSrcLoc.html)- SrcLoc
- A source-location mapping resulting from a compilation.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachTextSectionBuilder.html)- Text - Section - Builder
- Implementation of the `TextSectionBuilder`trait backed by`MachBuffer`.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/struct.MachTrap.html)- Trap
- A trap record resulting from a compilation.
- [Open](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenPatchRegion.html)- Patch - Region
- Represents the beginning of an editable region in the `MachBuffer``OpenPatchRegion``MachBuffer::end_patchable``OpenPatchRegion`
- [Patch](https://docs.rs/struct.PatchRegion.html)- Region
- A region in the `MachBuffer``MachBuffer::start_patchable``PatchRegion``MachBuffer::end_patchable``PatchRegion::patch`
- [RealReg](https://docs.rs/struct.RealReg.html)
- A real (physical) register. This corresponds to one of the target ISA’s named registers and can be used as an instruction operand.
- [Reg](https://docs.rs/struct.Reg.html)
- A register named in an instruction. This register can be a virtual
register, a fixed physical register, or a named spillslot (after
regalloc). It does not have any constraints applied to it: those
can be added later in `MachInst::get_operands()`when the`Reg`s are converted to`Operand`s.
- [Take](https://docs.rs/struct.TakeAndReplace.html)- AndReplace
- An RAII type to temporarily take a `U`out of a`T`and then put it back again on drop.
- [VCode](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstant.html)- Constant
- A use of a constant by one or more VCode instructions; see [VCodeConstants](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstants.html).
- [VCode](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstants.html)- Constants
- This structure tracks the large constants used in VCode that will be emitted separately by the
[MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html).
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.ValueLocRange.html)- LocRange
- Value location range.
- [Writable](https://docs.rs/struct.Writable.html)
- A type wrapper that indicates a register type is writable. The
underlying register can be extracted, and the type wrapper can be
built using an arbitrary register. Hence, this type-level wrapper
is not strictly a guarantee. However, “casting” to a writable
register is an explicit operation for which we can
audit. Ordinarily, internal APIs in the compiler backend should
take a `Writable<Reg>`whenever the register is written, and the usual, frictionless way to get one of these is to allocate a new temporary.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Codegen](https://docs.rs/enum.CodegenError.html)- Error
- A compilation error.
- [Exception](https://docs.rs/enum.ExceptionContextLoc.html)- Context - Loc
- A location for a dynamic exception context value.
- [Finalized](https://docs.rs/enum.FinalizedMachExceptionHandler.html)- Mach - Exception - Handler
- An item in the exception-handler list for a callsite, with final (lowered) code offsets. Items are interpreted in left-to-right order and the first match wins.
- [Finalized](https://docs.rs/enum.FinalizedRelocTarget.html)- Reloc - Target
- A Relocation target
- [Label](https://docs.rs/enum.LabelValueLoc.html)- Value - Loc
- The particular location for a value.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/enum.MachDebugTagPos.html)- Debug - TagPos
- Debug tag position on an instruction.
- [Reloc](https://docs.rs/enum.RelocDistance.html)- Distance
- Notion of “relocation distance”. This gives an estimate of how far away a symbol will be from a reference.
- [VCode](https://docs.rs/enum.VCodeConstantData.html)- Constant - Data
- Identify the different types of constant that can be inserted into [VCodeConstants](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstants.html). Tracking these separately instead of as raw byte buffers allows us to avoid some duplication.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [VERSION](https://docs.rs/constant.VERSION.html)
- Version number of this crate.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Mach](https://docs.rs/trait.MachInst.html)- Inst
- A machine instruction.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/trait.MachInstEmit.html)- Inst - Emit
- A trait describing the ability to encode a MachInst into binary machine code.
- [Mach](https://docs.rs/trait.MachInstEmitState.html)- Inst - Emit - State
- A trait describing the emission state carried between MachInsts when emitting a function body.
- [Text](https://docs.rs/trait.TextSectionBuilder.html)- Section - Builder
- An object that can be used to create the text section of an executable.
- [VCode](https://docs.rs/trait.VCodeInst.html)- Inst
- VCodeInst wraps all requirements for a MachInst to be in VCode: it must be
a `MachInst`and it must be able to emit itself at least to a`SizeCodeSink`.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Codegen](https://docs.rs/type.CodegenResult.html)- Result
- A convenient alias for a `Result`that uses`CodegenError`as the error type.
- [Compiled](https://docs.rs/type.CompiledCode.html)- Code
- `CompiledCode`in its final form (i.e. after- `FunctionParameters`have been applied), ready for consumption.
- [Finalized](https://docs.rs/type.FinalizedMachReloc.html)- Mach - Reloc
- A relocation resulting from a compilation.
- [FxHash](https://docs.rs/type.FxHashMap.html)- Map
- Type alias for a hash map that uses the Fx hashing algorithm.
- [FxHash](https://docs.rs/type.FxHashSet.html)- Set
- Type alias for a hash set that uses the Fx hashing algorithm.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/type.ValueLabelsRanges.html)- Labels - Ranges
- Resulting map of Value labels and their ranges/locations.

# cranelift_codegen::flowgraph - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/flowgraph/index.html

## Expand description

A control flow graph represented as mappings of basic blocks to their predecessors and successors.

Successors are represented as basic blocks while predecessors are represented by basic blocks. Basic blocks are denoted by tuples of block and branch/jump instructions. Each predecessor tuple corresponds to the end of a basic block.

```
    Block0:
        ...          ; beginning of basic block
        ...
        brif vx, Block1, Block2 ; end of basic block
    Block1:
        jump block3
```
Here `Block1` and `Block2` would each have a single predecessor denoted as `(Block0, brif)`,
while `Block3` would have a single predecessor denoted as `(Block1, jump block3)`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockPredecessor.html)- Predecessor
- A basic block denoted by its enclosing Block and last instruction.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlFlowGraph.html)- Flow - Graph
- The Control Flow Graph maintains a mapping of blocks to their predecessors and successors where predecessors are basic blocks and successors are basic blocks.
- [Pred](https://docs.rs/struct.PredIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator over block predecessors. The iterator type is `BlockPredecessor`.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Succ](https://docs.rs/type.SuccIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator over block successors. The iterator type is `Block`.

---

# cranelift_codegen::inline - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/inline/index.html

## Expand description

Function inlining infrastructure.

This module provides “inlining as a library” to Cranelift users; it does
*not* provide a complete, off-the-shelf inlining solution. Cranelift’s
compilation context is per-function and does not encompass the full call
graph. It does not know which functions are hot and which are cold, which
have been marked the equivalent of `#[inline(never)]`, etc… Only the
Cranelift user can understand these aspects of the full compilation
pipeline, and these things can be very different between (say) Wasmtime and
`cg_clif`. Therefore, this module does not attempt to define heuristics for
when inlining a particular call is likely beneficial. This module only
provides hooks for the Cranelift user to define whether a given call should
be inlined or not, and the mechanics to inline a callee into a particular
call site when directed to do so by the Cranelift user.

The top-level inlining entry point during Cranelift compilation is
[ Context::inline](https://docs.rs/struct.Context.html#method.inline). It takes an

[trait implementation, which is authored by the Cranelift user and directs Cranelift whether to inline a particular call, and, when inlining, gives Cranelift the body of the callee that is to be inlined.](https://docs.rs/trait.Inline.html)

`Inline`## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Inline](https://docs.rs/enum.InlineCommand.html)- Command
- A command directing Cranelift whether or not to inline a particular call.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Inline](https://docs.rs/trait.Inline.html)
- A trait for directing Cranelift whether to inline a particular call or not.

---

# cranelift_codegen::isa - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/isa/index.html

## Expand description

Instruction Set Architectures.

The `isa` module provides a `TargetIsa` trait which provides the behavior specialization needed
by the ISA-independent code generator. The sub-modules of this module provide definitions for
the instruction sets that Cranelift can target. Each sub-module has it’s own implementation of
`TargetIsa`.

[§](https://docs.rs#constructing-a-targetisa-instance)Constructing a `TargetIsa` instance

The target ISA is built from the following information:

- The name of the target ISA as a string. Cranelift is a cross-compiler, so the ISA to target can be selected dynamically. Individual ISAs can be left out when Cranelift is compiled, so a string is used to identify the proper sub-module.
- Values for settings that apply to all ISAs. This is represented by a `settings::Flags`instance.
- Values for ISA-specific settings.

The `isa::lookup()` function is the main entry point which returns an `isa::Builder`
appropriate for the requested ISA:

```
use cranelift_codegen::isa;
use cranelift_codegen::settings::{self, Configurable};
use core::str::FromStr;
use target_lexicon::Triple;
let shared_builder = settings::builder();
let shared_flags = settings::Flags::new(shared_builder);
match isa::lookup(triple!("x86_64")) {
    Err(_) => {
        // The x86_64 target ISA is not available.
    }
    Ok(mut isa_builder) => {
        isa_builder.set("use_popcnt", "on");
        let isa = isa_builder.finish(shared_flags);
    }
}
```
The configured target ISA trait object is a `Box<TargetIsa>` which can be used for multiple
concurrent function compilations.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [aarch64](https://docs.rs/aarch64/index.html)- `arm64`
- ARM 64-bit Instruction Set Architecture.
- [riscv64](https://docs.rs/riscv64/index.html)- `riscv64`
- risc-v 64-bit Instruction Set Architecture.
- [unwind](https://docs.rs/unwind/index.html)
- Represents information relating to function unwinding.
- [x64](https://docs.rs/x64/index.html)- `x86`
- X86_64-bit Instruction Set Architecture.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionAlignment.html)- Alignment
- Function alignment specifications as required by an ISA, returned by
`TargetIsa::function_alignment`
- [IsaBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.IsaBuilder.html)
- Builder for a `TargetIsa`. Modify the ISA-specific settings before creating the`TargetIsa`trait object with`finish`.
- [IsaFlags](https://docs.rs/struct.IsaFlagsHashKey.html)- Hash - Key
- A wrapper around the ISA-dependent flags types which only implements `Hash`.
- [Target](https://docs.rs/struct.TargetFrontendConfig.html)- Frontend - Config
- This struct provides information that a frontend may need to know about a target to produce Cranelift IR for the target.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.CallConv.html)- Conv
- Calling convention identifiers.
- [Lookup](https://docs.rs/enum.LookupError.html)- Error
- Describes reason for target lookup failure

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ALL_](https://docs.rs/constant.ALL_ARCHITECTURES.html)- ARCHITECTURES
- The string names of all the supported, but possibly not enabled, architectures. The elements of
this slice are suitable to be passed to the [lookup_by_name](https://docs.rs/fn.lookup_by_name.html)function to obtain the default configuration for that architecture.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Target](https://docs.rs/trait.TargetIsa.html)- Isa
- Methods that are specialized to a target ISA.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [lookup](https://docs.rs/fn.lookup.html)
- Look for an ISA for the given `triple`. Return a builder that can create a corresponding`TargetIsa`.
- [lookup_](https://docs.rs/fn.lookup_by_name.html)- by_ - name
- Look for a supported ISA with the given `name`. Return a builder that can create a corresponding`TargetIsa`.

# cranelift_codegen::packed_option - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/packed_option/index.html

## Expand description

Compact representation of `Option<T>` for types with a reserved value.

Small Cranelift types like the 32-bit entity references are often used in tables and linked
lists where an `Option<T>` is needed. Unfortunately, that would double the size of the tables
because `Option<T>` is twice as big as `T`.

This module provides a `PackedOption<T>` for types that have a reserved value that can be used
to represent `None`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Packed](https://docs.rs/struct.PackedOption.html)- Option
- Packed representation of `Option<T>`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Reserved](https://docs.rs/trait.ReservedValue.html)- Value
- Types that have a reserved value which can’t be created any other way.

---

# cranelift_codegen::settings - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/settings/index.html

## Expand description

Shared settings module.

This module defines data structures to access the settings defined in the meta language.

Each settings group is translated to a `Flags` struct either in this module or in its
ISA-specific `settings` module. The struct provides individual getter methods for all of the
settings as well as computed predicate flags.

The `Flags` struct is immutable once it has been created. A `Builder` instance is used to
create it.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cranelift_codegen::settings::{self, Configurable};
let mut b = settings::builder();
b.set("opt_level", "speed_and_size");
let f = settings::Flags::new(b);
assert_eq!(f.opt_level(), settings::OptLevel::SpeedAndSize);
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [detail](https://docs.rs/detail/index.html)
- Implementation details for generated code.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- Collect settings values based on a template.
- [Flags](https://docs.rs/struct.Flags.html)
- Flags group `shared`.
- [Flags](https://docs.rs/struct.FlagsOrIsa.html)- OrIsa
- Wrapper containing flags and optionally a `TargetIsa`trait object.
- [Setting](https://docs.rs/struct.Setting.html)
- Represents an available builder setting.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.Value.html)
- Represents a setting value.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- Values for `shared.libcall_call_conv`.
- [OptLevel](https://docs.rs/enum.OptLevel.html)
- Values for `shared.opt_level`.
- [Probestack](https://docs.rs/enum.ProbestackStrategy.html)- Strategy
- Values for `shared.probestack_strategy`.

- Values for `shared.regalloc_algorithm`.

- An error produced when changing a setting.

- Represents the kind of setting.

# cranelift_codegen::verifier - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/verifier/index.html

## Expand description

A verifier for ensuring that functions are well formed. It verifies:

block integrity

- All instructions reached from the `block_insts`iterator must belong to the block as reported by`inst_block()`.
- Every block must end in a terminator instruction, and no other instruction can be a terminator.
- Every value in the `block_params`iterator belongs to the block as reported by`value_block`.

Instruction integrity

- The instruction format must match the opcode.
- All result values must be created for multi-valued instructions.
- All referenced entities must exist. (Values, blocks, stack slots, …)
- Instructions must not reference (eg. branch to) the entry block.

SSA form

- Values must be defined by an instruction that exists and that is inserted in a block, or be an argument of an existing block.
- Values used by an instruction must dominate the instruction.

Control flow graph and dominator tree integrity:

- All predecessors in the CFG must be branches to the block.
- All branches to a block must be present in the CFG.
- A recomputed dominator tree is identical to the existing one.
- The entry block must not be a cold block.

Type checking

- Compare input and output values against the opcode’s type constraints. For polymorphic opcodes, determine the controlling type variable first.
- Branches and jumps must pass arguments to destination blocks that match the expected types exactly. The number of arguments must match.
- All blocks in a jump table must take no arguments.
- Function calls are type checked against their signature.
- The entry block must take arguments that match the signature of the current function.
- All return instructions must have return value operands matching the current function signature.

Global values

- Detect cycles in global values.
- Detect use of ‘vmctx’ global value when no corresponding parameter is defined.

Memory types

- Ensure that struct fields are in offset order.
- Ensure that struct fields are completely within the overall struct size, and do not overlap.

TODO: Ad hoc checking

- Stack slot loads and stores must be in-bounds.
- Immediate constraints for certain opcodes, like `iconst.i8 1234`.
- `Insertlane`and- `extractlane`instructions have immediate lane numbers that must be in range for their polymorphic type.
- Swizzle and shuffle instructions take a variable number of lane arguments. The number of arguments must match the destination type, and the lane indexes must be in range.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Verifier](https://docs.rs/struct.VerifierError.html)- Error
- A verifier error.
- [Verifier](https://docs.rs/struct.VerifierErrors.html)- Errors
- List of verifier errors.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [verify_](https://docs.rs/fn.verify_context.html)- context
- Verify `func`after checking the integrity of associated context data structures`cfg`and`domtree`.
- [verify_](https://docs.rs/fn.verify_function.html)- function
- Verify `func`.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Verifier](https://docs.rs/type.VerifierResult.html)- Result
- Result of a verification operation.
- [Verifier](https://docs.rs/type.VerifierStepResult.html)- Step - Result
- Result of a step in the verification process.

# cranelift_codegen::write - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/write/index.html

## Expand description

Converting Cranelift IR to text.

The `write` module provides the `write_function` function which converts an IR `Function` to an
equivalent textual form. This textual form can be read back by the `cranelift-reader` crate.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Plain](https://docs.rs/struct.PlainWriter.html)- Writer
- A `PlainWriter`that doesn’t decorate the function.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Func](https://docs.rs/trait.FuncWriter.html)- Writer
- A `FuncWriter`used to decorate functions during printing.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decorate_](https://docs.rs/fn.decorate_function.html)- function
- Writes `func`to`w`as text. write_function_plain is passed as ‘closure’ to print instructions as text. pretty_function_error is passed as ‘closure’ to add error decoration.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_block_header.html)- block_ - header
- Write out the basic block header, outdented:
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_function.html)- function
- Write `func`to`w`as equivalent text. Use`isa`to emit ISA-dependent annotations.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_function_spec.html)- function_ - spec
- Writes the spec (name and signature) of ‘func’ to ‘w’ as text.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_operands.html)- operands
- Write the operands of `inst`to`w`with a prepended space.

#### pub fn [compile](https://docs.rs#method.compile)(
    &mut self,
    isa: &dyn [TargetIsa](https://docs.rs/isa/trait.TargetIsa.html),
    ctrl_plane: &mut [ControlPlane](https://docs.rs/cranelift-control/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_control/zero_sized/struct.ControlPlane.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<&[CompiledCode](https://docs.rs/type.CompiledCode.html), [CompileError](https://docs.rs/struct.CompileError.html)<'_>>

Compile the function,

Run the function through all the passes necessary to generate
code for the target ISA represented by `isa`. The generated
machine code is not relocated. Instead, any relocations can be
obtained from `compiled_code.buffer.relocs()`.

Performs any optimizations that are enabled, unless
`optimize()` was already invoked.

Returns the generated machine code as well as information about the function’s code and read-only data.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/context.rs.html#231-233)use CompiledCode::get_code_bb_layout

use CompiledCode::get_code_bb_layout

If available, return information about the code layout in the final machine code: the offsets (in bytes) of each basic-block start, and all basic-block edges.

Replace all redundant loads with the known values in memory. These are loads whose values were already loaded by other loads earlier, as well as loads whose values were stored by a store instruction to the same instruction (so-called “store-to-load forwarding”).

# FinalizedMachCallSite in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.FinalizedMachCallSite.html

```
pub struct FinalizedMachCallSite<'a> {
    pub ret_addr:
```
[CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    pub frame_offset: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>,
    pub exception_handlers: &'a [[FinalizedMachExceptionHandler](https://docs.rs/enum.FinalizedMachExceptionHandler.html)],
}## Expand description

A call site record resulting from a compilation.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.ret_addr)

`ret_addr: `[CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html)The offset of the call’s return address, *relative to the
start of the buffer*.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.frame_offset)

`frame_offset: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>The offset from the FP at this callsite down to the SP when
the call occurs, if known. In other words, the size of the
stack frame up to the saved FP slot. Useful to recover the
start of the stack frame and to look up dynamic contexts
stored in [ ExceptionContextLoc::SPOffset](https://docs.rs/enum.ExceptionContextLoc.html#variant.SPOffset).

If `None`, the compiler backend did not specify a frame
offset. The runtime in use with the compiled code may require
the frame offset if exception handlers are present or dynamic
context is used, but that is not Cranelift’s concern: the
frame offset is optional at this level.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.exception_handlers)

`exception_handlers: &'a [`[FinalizedMachExceptionHandler](https://docs.rs/enum.FinalizedMachExceptionHandler.html)]Exception handlers at this callsite, with target offsets
*relative to the start of the buffer*.

# FrameLayout in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.FrameLayout.html

```
pub struct FrameLayout {
    pub word_bytes:
```
[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub incoming_args_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub tail_args_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub setup_area_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub clobber_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub fixed_frame_storage_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub stackslots_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub outgoing_args_size: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub clobbered_callee_saves: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Writable](https://docs.rs/struct.Writable.html)<[RealReg](https://docs.rs/struct.RealReg.html)>>,
    pub function_calls: FunctionCalls,
}## Expand description

Structure describing the layout of a function’s stack frame.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.word_bytes)

`word_bytes: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Word size in bytes, so this struct can be
monomorphic/independent of `ABIMachineSpec`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.incoming_args_size)

`incoming_args_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)N.B. The areas whose sizes are given in this structure fully cover the current function’s stack frame, from high to low stack addresses in the sequence below. Each size contains any alignment padding that may be required by the ABI. Size of incoming arguments on the stack. This is not technically part of this function’s frame, but code in the function will still need to access it. Depending on the ABI, we may need to set up a frame pointer to do so; we also may need to pop this area from the stack upon return.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.tail_args_size)

`tail_args_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The size of the incoming argument area, taking into account any
potential increase in size required for tail calls present in the
function. In the case that no tail calls are present, this value
will be the same as [ Self::incoming_args_size](https://docs.rs/struct.FrameLayout.html#structfield.incoming_args_size).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.setup_area_size)

`setup_area_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Size of the “setup area”, typically holding the return address and/or the saved frame pointer. This may be written either during the call itself (e.g. a pushed return address) or by code emitted from gen_prologue_frame_setup. In any case, after that code has completed execution, the stack pointer is expected to point to the bottom of this area. The same holds at the start of code emitted by gen_epilogue_frame_restore.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.clobber_size)

`clobber_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Size of the area used to save callee-saved clobbered registers. This area is accessed by code emitted from gen_clobber_save and gen_clobber_restore.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.fixed_frame_storage_size)

`fixed_frame_storage_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Storage allocated for the fixed part of the stack frame. This contains stack slots and spill slots.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.stackslots_size)

`stackslots_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The size of all stackslots.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.outgoing_args_size)

`outgoing_args_size: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Stack size to be reserved for outgoing arguments, if used by the current ABI, or 0 otherwise. After gen_clobber_save and before gen_clobber_restore, the stack pointer points to the bottom of this area.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.clobbered_callee_saves)

`clobbered_callee_saves: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Writable](https://docs.rs/struct.Writable.html)<[RealReg](https://docs.rs/struct.RealReg.html)>>Sorted list of callee-saved registers that are clobbered according to the ABI. These registers will be saved and restored by gen_clobber_save and gen_clobber_restore.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.function_calls)

`function_calls: FunctionCalls`The function’s call pattern classification.

# MachBuffer in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.MachBuffer.html

`pub struct MachBuffer<I: `[VCodeInst](https://docs.rs/trait.VCodeInst.html)> { /* private fields */ }## Expand description

A buffer of output to be produced, fixed up, and then emitted to a CodeSink in bulk.

This struct uses `SmallVec`s to support small-ish function bodies without
any heap allocation. As such, it will be several kilobytes large. This is
likely fine as long as it is stack-allocated for function emission then
thrown away; but beware if many buffer objects are retained persistently.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#500-1874)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-MachBuffer%3CI%3E)### impl<I: [VCodeInst](https://docs.rs/trait.VCodeInst.html)> [MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html)<I>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#500-1874)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-MachBuffer%3CI%3E)

### impl<I: [VCodeInst](https://docs.rs/trait.VCodeInst.html)> [MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html)<I>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#503-534)#### pub fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)() -> [MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html)<I>

#### pub fn [start_patchable](https://docs.rs#method.start_patchable)(&mut self) -> [OpenPatchRegion](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenPatchRegion.html)

Begin a region of patchable code. There is one requirement for the
code that is emitted: It must not introduce any instructions that
could be chomped (branches are an example of this). In other words,
you must not call [ MachBuffer::add_cond_branch](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html#method.add_cond_branch) or

[between calls to this method and](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html#method.add_uncond_branch)

`MachBuffer::add_uncond_branch`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html#method.end_patchable)

`MachBuffer::end_patchable`Allocate a `Label` to refer to some offset. May not be bound to a fixed
offset yet.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#704-723)#### pub fn [get_label_for_constant](https://docs.rs#method.get_label_for_constant)(&mut self, constant: [VCodeConstant](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstant.html)) -> [MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#704-723)

#### pub fn [get_label_for_constant](https://docs.rs#method.get_label_for_constant)(&mut self, constant: [VCodeConstant](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstant.html)) -> [MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html)

Returns a label that can be used to refer to the `constant` provided.

This will automatically defer a new constant to be emitted for
`constant` if it has not been previously emitted. Note that this
function may return a different label for the same constant at
different points in time. The label is valid to use only from the
current location; the MachBuffer takes care to emit the same constant
multiple times if needed so the constant is always in range.

Emit a reference to the given label with the given reference type (i.e., branch-instruction format) at the current offset. This is like a relocation, but handled internally.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#827-848)#### pub fn [add_uncond_branch](https://docs.rs#method.add_uncond_branch)(
    &mut self,
    start: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    end: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    target: [MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html),
)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#827-848)

#### pub fn [add_uncond_branch](https://docs.rs#method.add_uncond_branch)(
    &mut self,
    start: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    end: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    target: [MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html),
)

Inform the buffer of an unconditional branch at the given offset,
targeting the given label. May be used to optimize branches.
The last added label-use must correspond to this branch.
This must be called when the current offset is equal to `start`; i.e.,
before actually emitting the branch. This implies that for a branch that
uses a label and is eligible for optimizations by the MachBuffer, the
proper sequence is:

- Call `use_label_at_offset()`to emit the fixup record.
- Call `add_uncond_branch()`to make note of the branch.
- Emit the bytes for the branch’s machine code.

Additional requirement: no labels may be bound between `start` and `end`
(exclusive on both ends).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#856-890)#### pub fn [add_cond_branch](https://docs.rs#method.add_cond_branch)(

    target: [MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html),
    inverted: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#856-890)

This function returns a [ MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html) which will be the future address

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1358-1360)#### pub fn [emit_island](https://docs.rs#method.emit_island)(
    &mut self,

    ctrl_plane: &mut [ControlPlane](https://docs.rs/cranelift-control/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_control/zero_sized/struct.ControlPlane.html),
)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1358-1360)

#### pub fn [emit_island](https://docs.rs#method.emit_island)(
    &mut self,
    distance: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    ctrl_plane: &mut [ControlPlane](https://docs.rs/cranelift-control/0.133.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cranelift_control/zero_sized/struct.ControlPlane.html),
)

Emit all pending constants and required pending veneers.

Should only be called if `island_needed()` returns true, i.e., if we
actually reach a deadline. It’s not necessarily a problem to do so
otherwise but it may result in unnecessary work during emission.

The current code-emission position must be a “safe” location for an island: i.e., no fallthrough into the island contents from the previous instruction is possible. Callers emitting inside a basic block should emit a jump-around branch.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1825-1845)#### pub fn [push_user_stack_map](https://docs.rs#method.push_user_stack_map)(
    &mut self,
    emit_state: &I::[State](https://docs.rs/trait.MachInstEmit.html#associatedtype.State),
    return_addr: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    stack_map: [UserStackMap](https://docs.rs/ir/struct.UserStackMap.html),
)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1825-1845)

#### pub fn [push_user_stack_map](https://docs.rs#method.push_user_stack_map)(
    &mut self,
    emit_state: &I::[State](https://docs.rs/trait.MachInstEmit.html#associatedtype.State),
    return_addr: [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html),
    stack_map: [UserStackMap](https://docs.rs/ir/struct.UserStackMap.html),
)

Push a user stack map onto this buffer.

The stack map is associated with the given `return_addr` code
offset. This must be the PC for the instruction just *after* this stack
map’s associated instruction. For example in the sequence `call $foo; add r8, rax`, the `return_addr` must be the offset of the start of the
`add` instruction.

Stack maps must be pushed in sorted `return_addr` order.

Push a debug tag associated with the current buffer offset.

```
pub struct MachBufferFinalized<T: CompilePhase> {
    pub unwind_info:
```
[SmallVec](https://docs.rs/smallvec/1.15.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smallvec/struct.SmallVec.html)<[([CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html), [UnwindInst](https://docs.rs/isa/unwind/enum.UnwindInst.html)); [8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]>,
    pub alignment: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    pub nop_units: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>,
    /* private fields */
}## Expand description

A `MachBuffer` once emission is completed: holds generated code and records,
without fixups. This allows the type to be independent of the backend.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.unwind_info)

`unwind_info: `[SmallVec](https://docs.rs/smallvec/1.15.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smallvec/struct.SmallVec.html)<[([CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html), [UnwindInst](https://docs.rs/isa/unwind/enum.UnwindInst.html)); [8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]>Any unwind info at a given location.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.alignment)

`alignment: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The required alignment of this buffer.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.nop_units)

`nop_units: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>The means by which to NOP out patchable call sites.

This allows a consumer of a `MachBufferFinalized` to disable
patchable call sites (which are enabled by default) without
specific knowledge of the target ISA.

Each entry is one form of nop, and these are required to be sorted in ascending-size order.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1972-1983)

#### pub fn [call_sites](https://docs.rs#method.call_sites)(&self) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = [FinalizedMachCallSite](https://docs.rs/struct.FinalizedMachCallSite.html)<'_>> + '_

Get the list of call sites for this code, along with associated exception handlers.

Each item yielded by the returned iterator is a struct with:

- The call site metadata record, with a `ret_addr`field directly accessible and denoting the offset of the return address into this buffer’s code.
- The slice of pairs of exception tags and code offsets denoting exception-handler entry points associated with this call site.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1999-2001)#### pub fn [patchable_call_sites](https://docs.rs#method.patchable_call_sites)(
    &self,
) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = &MachPatchableCallSite> + '_

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#1999-2001)

#### pub fn [patchable_call_sites](https://docs.rs#method.patchable_call_sites)(
    &self,
) -> impl [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = &MachPatchableCallSite> + '_

Get the list of patchable call sites for this code.

Each location in the buffer contains the bytes for a call
instruction to the specified target. If the call is to be
patched out, the bytes in the region should be replaced with
those given in the `MachBufferFinalized::nop` array, repeated
as many times as necessary. (The length of the patchable
region is guaranteed to be an integer multiple of that NOP
unit size.)

# PatchRegion in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.PatchRegion.html

`pub struct PatchRegion { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A region in the [ MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html) code buffer that can be edited prior to finalization. An example
of where you might want to use this is for patching instructions that mention constants that
won’t be known until later:

[can be used to begin the patchable region, instructions can be emitted with placeholder constants, and the](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html#method.start_patchable)

`MachBuffer::start_patchable`[token can be produced by](https://docs.rs/struct.PatchRegion.html)

`PatchRegion`[. Once the values of those constants are known, the](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html#method.end_patchable)

`MachBuffer::end_patchable`[function can be used to get a mutable buffer to the instruction bytes, and the constants uses can be updated directly.](https://docs.rs/struct.PatchRegion.html#method.patch)

`PatchRegion::patch`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# Reg in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.Reg.html

`pub struct Reg(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A register named in an instruction. This register can be a virtual
register, a fixed physical register, or a named spillslot (after
regalloc). It does not have any constraints applied to it: those
can be added later in `MachInst::get_operands()` when the `Reg`s
are converted to `Operand`s.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

### impl [VCodeConstant](https://docs.rs/struct.VCodeConstant.html)

Return the raw bit encoding for this instance.

**Warning**: the raw bit encoding is opaque and has no
guaranteed correspondence to the entity’s index. It encodes the
entire state of this index value: either a valid index or an
invalid-index sentinel. The value returned by this method should
only be passed to `from_bits`.

Create a new instance from the raw bit encoding.

**Warning**: the raw bit encoding is opaque and has no
guaranteed correspondence to the entity’s index. It encodes the
entire state of this index value: either a valid index or an
invalid-index sentinel. The value returned by this method should
only be given bits from `as_bits`.

# VCodeConstants in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.VCodeConstants.html

`pub struct VCodeConstants { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

This structure tracks the large constants used in VCode that will be emitted separately by the
[MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html).

First, during the lowering phase, constants are inserted using
[VCodeConstants.insert]; an intermediate handle, `VCodeConstant`, tracks what constants are
used in this phase. Some deduplication is performed, when possible, as constant
values are inserted.

Secondly, during the emission phase, the [MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html) assigns [MachLabel](https://docs.rs/struct.MachLabel.html)s for each of the
constants so that instructions can refer to the value’s memory location. The [MachBuffer](https://docs.rs/struct.MachBuffer.html)
then writes the constant values to the buffer.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# Writable in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/struct.Writable.html

Struct Writable  Copy item path  Source  `pub struct Writable<T> {  }`Expand description A type wrapper that indicates a register type is writable. The
underlying register can be extracted, and the type wrapper can be
built using an arbitrary register. Hence, this type-level wrapper
is not strictly a guarantee. However, “casting” to a writable
register is an explicit operation for which we can
audit. Ordinarily, internal APIs in the compiler backend should
take a `Writable<Reg>` whenever the register is written, and the
usual, frictionless way to get one of these is to allocate a new
temporary.

Explicitly construct a `Writable<T>` from a `T`. As noted in
the documentation for `Writable`, this is not hidden or
disallowed from the outside; anyone can perform the “cast”;
but it is explicit so that we can audit the use sites.

Get the underlying register, which can be read.

Get a mutable borrow of the underlying register.

Map the underlying register to another value or type.

Return the register’s hardware encoding; e.g., `0` for `%rax`.

Return the register name.

Create a register from its hardware encoding.

pub enum CodegenError {

```
[VerifierErrors](https://docs.rs/verifier/struct.VerifierErrors.html)),
    ImplLimitExceeded,
    CodeTooLarge,
    Unsupported([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)),
    RegisterMappingError([RegisterMappingError](https://docs.rs/isa/unwind/systemv/enum.RegisterMappingError.html)),
    Regalloc([CheckerErrors](https://docs.rs/regalloc2/0.15.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/regalloc2/checker/struct.CheckerErrors.html)),
}## Expand description

A compilation error.

When Cranelift fails to compile a function, it will return one of these error codes.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Verifier)

### Verifier([VerifierErrors](https://docs.rs/verifier/struct.VerifierErrors.html))

A list of IR verifier errors.

This always represents a bug, either in the code that generated IR for Cranelift, or a bug in Cranelift itself.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ImplLimitExceeded)

### ImplLimitExceeded

An implementation limit was exceeded.

Cranelift can compile very large and complicated functions, but the [implementation has
limits](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/blob/main/cranelift/docs/ir.md#implementation-limits) that cause compilation to fail when they are exceeded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CodeTooLarge)

### CodeTooLarge

The code size for the function is too large.

Different target ISAs may impose a limit on the size of a compiled function. If that limit is exceeded, compilation fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unsupported)

### Unsupported([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))

Something is not supported by the code generator. This might be an indication that a feature is used without explicitly enabling it, or that something is temporarily unsupported by a given target backend.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RegisterMappingError)

### RegisterMappingError([RegisterMappingError](https://docs.rs/isa/unwind/systemv/enum.RegisterMappingError.html))

**crate feature**only.

`unwind`A failure to map Cranelift register representation to a DWARF register representation.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Regalloc)

### Regalloc([CheckerErrors](https://docs.rs/regalloc2/0.15.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/regalloc2/checker/struct.CheckerErrors.html))

Register allocator internal error discovered by the symbolic checker.

# FinalizedMachExceptionHandler in cranelift_codegen - Rust

```
pub enum FinalizedMachExceptionHandler {
    Tag(
```
[ExceptionTag](https://docs.rs/ir/entities/struct.ExceptionTag.html), [CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html)),
    Default([CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html)),

}## Expand description

An item in the exception-handler list for a callsite, with final (lowered) code offsets. Items are interpreted in left-to-right order and the first match wins.

A specific tag (in the current dynamic context) should be handled by the code at the given offset.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Default)

### Default([CodeOffset](https://docs.rs/binemit/type.CodeOffset.html))

All exceptions should be handled by the code at the given offset.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Context)

### Context([ExceptionContextLoc](https://docs.rs/enum.ExceptionContextLoc.html))

The dynamic context for interpreting tags is updated to the value stored in the given machine location (in this frame’s context).

# MachDebugTagPos in cranelift_codegen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cranelift-codegen/0.133.1/cranelift_codegen/enum.MachDebugTagPos.html

```
pub enum MachDebugTagPos {
    Post,
    Pre,
}
```
## Expand description

Debug tag position on an instruction.

We need to distinguish position on an instruction, and not just use offsets, because of the following case:

```
<tag1, tag2> call ...
<tag3, tag4> trapping_store ...
```
If the stack is walked and interpreted with debug tags while within the call, the PC seen will be the return point, i.e. the address after the call. If the stack is walked and interpreted with debug tags upon a trap of the following instruction, it will be the PC of that instruction – which is the same PC! Thus to disambiguate which tags we want, we attach a “pre/post” flag to every group of tags at an offset; and when we look up tags, we look them up for an offset and “position” at that offset.

Thus there are logically two positions at every offset – so the above will be emitted as

```
0: call ...
                         4, post: <tag1, tag2>
                         4, pre: <tag3, tag4>
4: trapping_store ...
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Post)

### Post

Tags attached after the instruction that ends at this offset.

This is used to attach tags to a call, because the PC we see
when walking the stack is the *return point*.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Pre)

### Pre

Tags attached before the instruction that starts at this offset.

This is used to attach tags to every other kind of instruction, because the PC we see when processing a trap of that instruction is the PC of that instruction, not the following one.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/buffer.rs.html#2423)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/mod.rs.html#279)#### fn [get_operands](https://docs.rs#tymethod.get_operands)(&mut self, collector: &mut impl OperandVisitor)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/cranelift_codegen/machinst/mod.rs.html#279)

#### fn [get_operands](https://docs.rs#tymethod.get_operands)(&mut self, collector: &mut impl OperandVisitor)

Return the registers referenced by this machine instruction along with the modes of reference (use, def, modify).

If this is a simple move, return the (source, destination) tuple of registers.

Is this a terminator (branch or ret)? If so, return its type (ret/uncond/cond) and target if applicable.

Classify the type of call instruction this is.

This enables more granular function type analysis and optimization.
Returns `CallType::None` for non-call instructions, `CallType::Regular`
for normal calls that return to the caller, and `CallType::TailCall`
for tail calls that don’t return to the caller.
